etymology: English: the hour after the last deadline, when the week's worst news gets filed.
trigger: A story that has to be released and must not be discussed.
tell: A 5:40 p.m. Friday email, a PDF with no summary, and a press office that has stopped answering the phone.
counter: Read it on Saturday. Publish the number rather than the timing - the dump only works if the story is allowed to arrive on its own schedule.

confused_with.tell: The nonpology buries the harm in the wording; the dump buries it in the timing.

senses: The move of releasing inconvenient information at the end of the week, when the audience is gone and the reporters who remain are tired.

It works because attention has a shape. Friday evening is the bottom of the news week, and a story that lands there gets one cycle instead of five - so the document is public and unnoticed at the same time, which is the whole design.

notes.label: Bent by the feed
notes.text: The feed has bent this rather than broken it: the release is now permanent and searchable, so the dump no longer hides the story, it only starves it of the attention it would have had.

example: *"The settlement went out at 5:47 on a Friday, in a **Friday news dump** with a cover note that said 'for immediate release'."*
